title: FlashDecoding++: Faster Large Language Model Inference on GPUs
technique: Asynchronized softmax with unified max value; flat-GEMM with double buffering (pad to 8 not 64); heuristic dataflow selection among kernels by shape/hardware

optimized_metrics.evidence: To tackle these challenges and enable a faster Large Language Model (LLM) inference, we present FlashDecoding++ in this paper.

(2) Under-utilized computation of flat GEMM. The shape of matrices performing GEMM in LLM inference is flat, leading to under-utilized computation and >50% performance loss after padding zeros in previous designs
many works focus on improving the throughput of generating tokens (i.e., reducing latency of each token)

optimized_metrics.evidence_note: weak design evidence: sentence frames decode-phase goal (reducing latency of each token); no explicit statistic stated

headline_claim.text: FlashDecoding++ can achieve up to 4.86× and 3.93× speedup on both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs compared to Hugging Face implementations. FlashDecoding++ also achieves an average speedup of 1.37× compared to state-of-the-art LLM inference engines on mainstream LLMs.

Fig 1 right, Fig 11 (prefill first-token latency ms)

extractor_notes: Kernel/engine-level: the design targets kernel utilization and per-engine decode/prefill speed (speedup), not serving metrics under load. No SLO, no percentiles, no queueing.
